title: Heating curve: ice at −10 °C to steam at 100 °C
caption: For 0.5 kg: warming the ice takes 10.5 kJ, melting 167 kJ, warming the water 209 kJ and boiling 1130 kJ, a total of 1517 kJ. The sloping parts have gradient 1/(mc); the flat plateaus are the latent heats, where energy goes into the bonds and the temperature stays put. Boiling alone is 75% of the total.
alt: Graph of temperature against energy supplied: a short slope from −10 to 0 °C, a plateau at 0 °C to 178 kJ, a slope to 100 °C at 387 kJ, then a long plateau at 100 °C ending at 1517 kJ.
description: The horizontal axis is the energy supplied in kJ; the vertical axis is the temperature in °C.
Ice warms from −10 to 0 °C: Q = 0.5 × 2100 × 10 = 10.5 kJ.
Melting at 0 °C: Q = mL = 0.5 × 334 = 167 kJ, a flat plateau.
Boiling at 100 °C: 0.5 × 2260 = 1130 kJ, the longest plateau. Total ≈ 1517 kJ.

checks.name: the water starts at 0 °C after 178 kJ (melting took 167 kJ)
